[warmly] Hello E2E Driver! It sounds like you are teaching the concept of fractions through a very interactive and relatable approach. Using a circle divided into four parts and coloring one part helps students visualize what a fraction really means. Your connection to everyday examples like sharing a cake makes the abstract idea concrete for young learners. 

[thoughtfully] One suggestion is to clarify the definition of a fraction a bit more simply—something like “a fraction shows how many parts of a whole you have.” Also, when you mention numbers above and below like 3/4 or 9/10, it’s great to connect it to real-life experiences like test scores, but maybe slow down a little so students can follow the idea of numerator and denominator clearly.

[encouragingly] Overall, your storytelling and use of questions keep students engaged and thinking. Keep weaving those practical examples and encouraging them to explain in their own words. This builds deep understanding and confidence. You’re doing a fantastic job! If you want, I can help you develop a step-by-step lesson plan or some visual aids to support this topic. Just let me know!
